'''''Coreopsis lanceolata''''', commonly known as '''lanceleaf coreopsis''',<ref name=":0" /> '''lanceleaf tickseed''',<ref name="usda">{{Cite PLANTS |symbol=COLA5 |taxon=Coreopsis lanceolata}}</ref> '''lance-leaved coreopsis''',<ref name=":1" /> or '''sand coreopsis''',<ref name="natureserve">{{cite web |title=NatureServe Explorer 2.0 |url=https://explorer.natureserve.org/Taxon/ELEMENT_GLOBAL.2.140944/Coreopsis_lanceolata |website=explorer.natureserve.org}}</ref> is a [[North America]]n [[species]] of [[Coreopsis|tickseed]] in the family [[Asteraceae]].

==Description==
''Coreopsis lanceolata'' is a [[perennial plant]] sometimes attaining a height of over {{convert |60|cm|ft|0|abbr=on|}}. The plant produces yellow flower heads singly at the top of a naked flowering stalk, each head containing both [[ray florets]] and [[disc floret]]s.<ref>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=200023717 Flora of North America, ''Coreopsis lanceolata'' Linnaeus, Sp. Pl. 2: 908. 1753. ]</ref> Each flower measures {{convert |2-3|in|cm|0|order=flip|abbr=on|}} across. Basal [[Leaf|leaves]] are typically narrow, lance-shaped, and {{convert |2-6|in|cm|0|order=flip|abbr=on|}} long with smooth margins. They have thin [[Petiole (botany)|petioles]] that are {{convert |1-4|in|cm|0|order=flip|abbr=on|}} long. Leaves higher up the stem are [[sessility (botany)|sessile]] and may be unlobed or pinnately lobed.<ref name=":0" /> The stem leaves are opposite and generally appear only on the lower half of the stem. After flowering, the ray florets are replaced by brown [[achenes]] that are {{convert |3|mm|in|1|abbr=on|}} long and {{convert |3|mm|in|1|abbr=on|}} across.<ref name="IL"/>

==Etymology==
The genus name ''Coreopsis'' means "bug-like"; it comes from the Greek words "koris", meaning "bug" and "opsis", meaning "like". The genus name, as well as the common name, tickseed, comes from the fact that the seeds are small and resemble ticks. The specific epithet ''lanceolata'' refers to the shape of the leaves.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Coreopsis lanceolata - Plant Finder|url=https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=277306&isprofile=1&basic=coreopsis%20lanceolata|access-date=2021-02-20|website=www.missouribotanicalgarden.org}}</ref>

==As an invasive plant outside of USA==
Introduced to Japan and China as an ornamental species and later used extensively in greenification projects, particularly along river banks and railways, ''Coreopsis lanceolata'' is now known to be outcompeting native plant life and has since 2006 been labeled an invasive species by the Invasive Alien Species Act. The cultivation, transplantation, sale, or purchase of ''Coreopsis lanceolata'' is now prohibited and the plant has become the subject of a nationwide destruction campaign, even earning a spot on the Ecological Society of Japan's 100 Worst Invasive Species list.<ref name=robin>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=200023717 Flora of China, <big>剑叶金鸡菊</big> jian ye jin ji ju, ''Coreopsis lanceolata'' Linnaeus]</ref><ref name="B1">{{cite book | author = 多紀保彦 |script-title=ja:日本の外来生物: 決定版 | publisher = [[:ja:平凡社]] | date = 2008-04-21 | isbn = 978-4-582-54241-7 }}</ref><ref name="Rdoco">{{Cite journal|author=畠瀬頼子 |script-title=ja:オオキンケイギク(Coreopsis lanceolata L.)(緑化植物ど・こ・ま・で・き・わ・め・る) |date=2009-02-28 |script-journal=ja:日本緑化工学会誌 |volume=34 |number=3 }}</ref><ref name="Rbunpu">{{Cite journal |author=畠瀬頼子 |author2=小栗ひとみ |author3=松江正彦|year=2008|script-title=ja:木曽川中流域における植生変遷と特定外来生物オオキンケイギクの分布特性 |script-journal=ja:ランドスケープ研究 |volume=71 |issue=5 |pages=553–556}}</ref>
The species is also considered an invasive weed in Eastern Australia.<ref name=lucid>[https://keyserver.lucidcentral.org/weeds/data/media/Html/coreopsis_lanceolata.htm Coreopsis lanceolate lucid central weeds]</ref>

==Ecology==
Flowers bloom April to June.<ref name=":1" /> Many insects are attracted to the plant's nectar and pollen, including bees, wasps, butterflies, moths, flies, and beetles.<ref name="IL">{{cite web |title=Sand Coreopsis (Coreopsis lanceolata) |url=https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/prairie/plantx/sand_coreopsisx.htm |website=www.illinoiswildflowers.info}}</ref> Birds and small mammals eat the achenes.<ref>{{cite web |title=Tickseed Coreopsis |url=https://mdc.mo.gov/discover-nature/field-guide/tickseed-coreopsis |website=Missouri Department of Conservation |language=en}}</ref> The plant can spread to form colonies.<ref name="IL"/>

==Cultivation==
''Coreopsis lanceolata'' is useful for pollinator restoration in large urban cities, providing a food source for animals that drink the nectar and/or eat the seed. The plant should not be over watered as it will flop over. It may be restricted by growing in containers or in lawns that tend to be mowed. It requires little maintenance, although [[deadheading (flowers)|deadheading]] is beneficial.

It prefers a sandy, well-drained soil.<ref name=":0" />  Heavy, clay-based soil retains moisture in winter months, which can kill many species. However, because ''C. lanceolata'' is [[rhizomatous]] (having underground stems), it is well-adapted to withstand extremes in soil moisture (both wet and dry). Adding compost to heavy soil can improve drainage as can creating a mounded bed, allowing the planting area to shed rain faster than the ground around it. It thrives in full sun (4–6 hours of direct sunlight per day).
